newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Capital Intelligence rates two Indian banks.
newsitem.headline: Capital Intelligence rates two Indian banks.

text.p: Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence on Friday assigned initial ratings of BBB long-term and A-2 short term to India's HDFC Bank Ltd.
The agency, which specialises in bank ratings, also assigned initial ratings of BB long-term and A-3 short-term to Global Trust Bank Ltd.
A press release from Capital Intelligence said both banks have been assigned a stable outlook.

Capital Intelligence said that over the past two years HDFC Bank has built up an impressive list of blue chip corporate customers. "It has strong foreign exchange operations and has developed a promising custody services business," said Capital Intelligence.
But it said in common with other new banks, HDFC Bank is hampered by the limited reach of its small 20-branch network and its stable deposit base continues to be inefficient.

HDFC Bank was established in January 1995 by India's premier real estate morgage company, the Housing Development Finance Corporation which has a 26 percent stake in the bank. HDFC's other major shareholder is NatWest Markets, the investment banking division of the National Westminster Bank Plc., which owns 20 percent of the equity.
HDFC Bank had total assets of $289 million at the end of March 1996.

The Global Trust Bank is fully automated and benefits from low staffing levels and high productivity. The bank focusses primarily on the export sector which recieves government support, including guarantees from state institutions.

However, said Capital Intelligence, the withdrawal of official re-finance for export credit last year resulted in some uncertainties for the bank as it had to replace these funds with alternative sources of funding.
Its principal promoters, Mr. R Gelli and Mr. S Subasri, are capable professional bankers with strong track records, Capital Intelligence said.
The Global Trust Bank is the largest of the new banks in India with total assets of US$657 million at the end of September 1996. It currently operates 25 branches across the country.
